newsitem.title: UK: Marks to open second City of London store.
newsitem.headline: Marks to open second City of London store.

text.p: Retailer Marks and Spencer Plc said on Wednesday it would open its second major store in London's financial district after exchanging contracts with Barclays Property Holdings on a site at 168 Fenchurch Street in the City of London.
BPH has already started demolishing the bank which stood on the site, and this is due to be completed by the spring of 1998.
M&S has not got planning permission yet for the store, but a spokeswoman said the company was confident this would be forthcoming.
The retailer would not put a figure on the deal, but said it was part of M&S's 1.5 billion stg capital expenditure programme over three years.

The new store will have 75,000 square feet of selling space, making it bigger than M&S's existing store in the City on Finsbury Pavement, which has 53,000 square feet. It will carry a wide range of clothing, footwear, home furnishings and food.

M&S estates director Roger Aldridge said, "Our first store in the City at Finsbury Pavement has been a fantastic success, and the acquisition of the Barclays site gives us a prime location from which to improve our service." --London Newsroom + 44 171 542 7717
